newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: It's all over, Bangladesh's Ershad tells lover.
newsitem.headline: It's all over, Bangladesh's Ershad tells lover.

text.p: Bangladesh's former military ruler Hossain Mohammad Ershad has severed all ties with his lover of 14 years, bowing to pressure from his family and party, a statement by his Jatiya Party said on Thursday. The news comes a day after reports that Ershad, 68, was in a bind over the affair, having to choose between his lover and fiancee Zinat Hossain, who is in her late 40s, and his political career.

"Party chairman Hossain Mohammad Ershad has said he has no relationship anymore with Zinat Hossain and that she has been asked to refrain from all activities of the Jatiya party," said the statement published in Thursday's newspapers.

Ershad had decided to cut all ties with Zinat, a fellow Jatiya party member, in view of recent "confusion and misunderstanding" about his relationship with the wife of former Industry Secretary Mosharraf Hossain, the Jatiya Party's Daily Janata said.

The Banglabazar Patrika, a leading Dhaka daily, said Ershad had asked Zinat to leave the country for a while to allow him to calm political colleagues angered by the affair and reorganise the party. Zinat was not immediately available for comment.
Ershad told the Sangbad newspaper on Tuesday: "My relationship with Zinat has been a 14-year affair. She has done a lot for me ... I want to make a decision about her.
"My problem is now is one lady (Zinat), I feel very weak at this. And I don't know how to overcome it," Ershad said.
"I have made my proposal (of marriage) to Zinat and am awaiting her reply," he added.
Newspapers on Wednesday said Zinat had told Ershad he must divorce his wife Begum Roushan, his wife of more than 40 years, before they can wed.
Lieutenant-General Ershad, who seized power in 1982, was deposed in 1990 and was in jail until January when he was freed on bail.
He stirred controversy when he celebrated his birthday recently with Zinat instead of his wife.
Close associates in the Jatiya Party objected to such behaviour and three Jatiya leaders told newspapers on Wednesday they might break with Ershad and even split the party.
Ershad started bowing to pressure on Wednesday night, telling his followers that "politics is my first love".
A Jatiya Party leader said: "The chairman (Ershad) assured us that he would do nothing that harms the party and makes his political future uncertain."
